title: From the cracks of the earth (Kern ch. 14)
word: From the cracks of the earth
hook: countless bodhisattvas rise from the ground, pupils of the Buddha from long ago
tomorrow: The lifespan of the Tathagata (Kern ch. 15)

segments.voice: Yesterday, four ways to teach calmly, and a king who kept one jewel in his hair for the deed beyond all others. Your line: the jewel in the topknot.

In spring, a crack in the sidewalk fills with green. Nobody planted it or watered it. It was down there all along, working in the dark, and one day it's just up. Chapter fourteen of the Lotus Sutra opens with an offer of help. Bodhisattvas from other worlds say to the Buddha: let us protect this sutra here after you're gone. A generous offer, and a sensible one. The Buddha turns it down. No need, he says. This world already has its own. Then the ground starts to split.
screen: `GREEN IN A SIDEWALK CRACK.` → `AN OFFER OF HELP.` → `NO NEED.`

segments.voice: First, the refusal. The visitors mean well, but this world has bodhisattvas of its own who will keep the sutra after him. Second, the earth opens. All across this world the ground cracks, and up rise bodhisattvas beyond counting, bodies shining gold, each with a great company of followers. They go up to the jeweled stupa still hanging in the sky and bow to the two Buddhas seated there. Four lead them, and all four names speak of conduct: superior, boundless, pure, and firm. Third, nobody knows them. Maitreya, who is said to be the next Buddha, has never seen a single one, and neither has anyone else. Who are these? The Buddha answers: I taught them, all of them, here in this world since my awakening. They've lived below, studying quietly, away from crowds. Fourth, the puzzle. Maitreya is honest about how strange that sounds. You awakened not long ago; how could you have taught so many? It's like a young man with dark hair pointing at white-haired elders and saying, these are my sons, while they nod and say, he's our father. Who would believe it? The chapter ends with that question in the air, and tomorrow answers it. This is the week's last day, so lay its chapters side by side: the attendant and the son, the one who teaches a single verse, a girl from under the sea, two women waiting to be named, and now a crowd nobody knew was there. All week, the Lotus kept counting the people nobody was counting.
screen: `VISITORS OFFER TO HELP.` · `NO NEED: THE EARTH OPENS.` · `I TAUGHT THEM ALL.` · `A YOUNG MAN WITH OLD SONS.` · then, large: `THEY ROSE FROM THE EARTH.`

segments.voice: Feel the ground holding you up, and bring to mind one thing in your life that grew while nobody was watching: a friendship that deepened without a big moment, a child suddenly taller, a patience you didn't have a few years ago. Notice how long it was working underground before it showed, and rest with it.
From the cracks of the earth. Bodhisattvas beyond counting, taught by the Buddha in this world, rise from beneath it when he says no outside help is needed. Today's word.
screen: `FROM THE CRACKS OF THE EARTH — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: they rose from the earth. Nobody knew they were there. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-nine, done.

screen: `DAY 1169 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE LIFESPAN OF THE TATHAGATA (KERN CH. 15).`

howItsDone: In Mahayana communities that read the Lotus Sutra, the bodhisattvas who rise from the earth are honored as the ones entrusted with the sutra in this world, and some schools, including Nichiren Buddhism, give them and their leader a central place.

what it means: bodhisattvas the Buddha taught in this world, living quietly below it, rise when he says no outside help is needed.
what a scholar hears: Maitreya's puzzle, a young father with aged sons, sets up the next chapter's answer about how long the Buddha has really lived.

chat.says: Why does the Buddha turn down help from those visiting bodhisattvas?
options: This world already has its own: countless bodhisattvas he taught rise up from the earth.
He doesn't want the sutra kept by anyone at all once he's gone from this world.
The visitors were unkind, so he sends them back home as a warning to the rest.
chat.meaning: In chapter fourteen the Buddha says this world has its own. Bodhisattvas beyond counting rise from the earth, all taught by him here.

Maitreya.meaning: the bodhisattva said to be the next Buddha

stupa.meaning: a tower built to hold the remains of a holy one
